correctness.rationale: The proof differentiates the exact two-branch formula at the unique crossing. At the crossing, the derivative of the branch-power difference reduces to a positive-weighted digamma/integral expression. The inequalities \(q/(1+q)<1/6\), \(\psi(p+1)<7/5\), \(-J'(p)/J(p)<1/3\), and \(\log(e/2)>3/10\) give \(h'(p_0)/\Gamma(p_0+1)<-1/90\). The identity \(h'(p_0)=p_0 C_{p_0}^{p_0-1}(A'(p_0)-B'(p_0))\) then gives the stated derivative jump. All quantifiers and the dependence on the source bracket \(p_0\in(2.9414,2.9415)\) are explicit. The packaged checker reproduces the crossing and derivative ordering numerically but is not used as the proof.

value.rationale: The source presents the change of sharp extremizer as a phase transition. Determining whether the two optimal branches meet tangentially or transversely is a natural structural question about that transition. The result proves a quantitative first-order cusp, showing robustness of the branch switch and giving an explicit sensitivity scale. This is not a parameter substitution or table recomputation; it distinguishes a genuine first-order transition from higher-order contact.
